subject: Clearedge OneTrust incremental import — failover & stitch plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@clearedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@clearedge.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: OneTrust incremental import errors

Hi Jordan,

We're in the middle of importing the Clearedge security profile to OneTrust and are seeing a series of partial failures in the incremental import step (some CAIQ/SIG fragments are rejected with 400/422). The UI shows the most recent manifest as processed, but the evidence delta is missing several S3 objects.

Quick context: we used your presign workflow and uploaded a tarball of artifacts. The import summary shows 62/78 fragments accepted and 16 failed with a "missing_resource" error. Attached is the import log we downloaded from the portal (s3_presign_log.txt).

Can you advise on an immediate mitigation path? Ideally we want: a) identify which objects are missing vs malformed, b) a fallback re-ingest for only the failed fragments, and c) guidance so we don't have to re-run the full upload.

Thanks — appreciate a fast look.

-elena
Elena Park
Head of Security Operations, Clearedge Financial
elena.park@clearedge.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: s3_presign_log.txt
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@clearedge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: OneTrust incremental import errors

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads-up and the log. I dug into the portal trace and here's what I propose as a short remediation path so you avoid a full re-upload: 

1) Quick triage (we did this): the 16 failures map to three presign timeouts and a handful of path-encoding mismatches (spaces and special chars in object keys). I attached a short stitch plan that enumerates the affected object keys and a two-step re-ingest approach.

2) Failover re-ingest: we'll produce a minimal manifest that contains only the failed fragments and a presign window of 60 minutes. You can upload the delta tarball to the same bucket; OneTrust will accept an import referencing the new manifest.

3) Prevent recurrence: Kimberly will confirm the presign policy (content-type enforcement + max key length) and we'll add a lightweight client-side validator to our upload helper.

Next steps:
- Elena: please confirm you can re-run an upload during our presign window (I can schedule a 30-min window tomorrow morning).
- Kimberly/Rishi: can you review the attached stitch_plan.md and confirm we can generate the minimal manifest from the portal import id (ABC123) without changing the record?

I'll schedule a 10–15 min screen-share if that helps.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0133

Attachments: stitch_plan.md
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: OneTrust incremental import errors (internal)

Jordan / Rishi — quick internal note:

- The presign policy currently enforces strict content-type and normalizes keys by URL-encoding at generation time. The mismatch you saw is consistent with uploads that bypassed our client helper (some partners use curl/sftp wrappers).
- We can create a minimal manifest by querying the import job (import id ABC123) and composing a delta bundle. That avoids touching the original import record.
- Two operational asks before we issue a new presign window:
  * Confirm Clearedge can complete the upload within 60 minutes (Jordan to confirm scheduling).
  * We need a transient role grant on the target bucket to validate object existence post-upload; otherwise we rely on OneTrust's import webhook.

I'll stand up the presign with the encoding-aware generator (adds an extra step to percent-encode keys we flag). Rishi — can you confirm that granting the transient read role to our ingestion lambda for the 2-hour window is okay from infra/security? If not, we'll fallback to webhook verification.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security Enablement, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@clearedge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: OneTrust incremental import errors — resolution

Elena — quick update and resolution summary: 

Thanks for running the delta upload this morning. The minimal manifest re-ingest succeeded and OneTrust accepted the remaining 16 fragments.

What we did:
- Issued a 60-minute presign window tied to a delta manifest (import ABC123-delta).
- Applied an encoding normalization pass in the presign generator for the flagged keys.
- Temporarily granted a transient read role to our ingestion lambda to validate object existence after upload; we revoked the role immediately after validation.

Post-mortem notes for your team:
- Two uploads used legacy tools that did not URL-encode keys; recommend updating any scripted upload helpers to our client validator.
- We attached the stitch plan we used and the condensed import log.

Attachments: evidence_manifest.csv, stitch_plan.md

If you want, we can run a lightning session with your Ops engineers to walk through the presign client and the encoding checks. Happy to coordinate calendars.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0133
